description: Step-by-step response to a ransomware incident from detection through recovery and reporting.

steps.description: Detect and confirm that a ransomware incident is underway by analyzing alerts, file encryption patterns, and ransom notes.

inputs.name: alert-data
inputs.desc: Security alerts or user reports indicating possible ransomware

inputs.name: affected-system-info
inputs.desc: Hostname, IP, OS, and role of the affected system

outputs.name: confirmation-report
outputs.desc: Confirmed or ruled-out ransomware determination with evidence

outputs.name: ransomware-variant-id
outputs.desc: Identified ransomware family and variant if known

process: Review the alert or user report for ransomware indicators (encrypted files, ransom note, unusual extensions)
Check endpoint detection logs for process activity associated with encryption
Identify the ransomware variant using ransom note text, file extensions, or hash lookups
Document the confirmation with timestamps and evidence

steps.description: Isolate affected systems to prevent the ransomware from spreading to additional hosts.

outputs.name: isolation-log
outputs.desc: Record of all isolation actions taken with timestamps

outputs.name: scope-assessment
outputs.desc: Preliminary scope of affected vs unaffected systems

process: Disconnect affected systems from the network (disable ports, remove from VLAN, or use EDR isolation)
Disable any shared drives or mapped network paths accessible from infected hosts
Block lateral movement by restricting SMB and RDP at the firewall for affected subnets
Document each isolation action and the time it was performed

steps.description: Preserve volatile and non-volatile evidence from affected systems before recovery begins.

inputs.name: scope-assessment
inputs.desc: List of affected systems to capture evidence from

outputs.name: evidence-inventory
outputs.desc: Cataloged and hashed evidence items

outputs.name: memory-dumps
outputs.desc: Memory captures from affected systems

process: Capture memory from affected systems before powering down (using tools like WinPmem or LiME)
Image affected disks or create forensic copies of encrypted volumes
Collect relevant logs (event logs, EDR telemetry, firewall logs)
Hash all collected evidence and record in a chain-of-custody log

steps.description: Determine the full scope of the ransomware impact across the environment.

outputs.name: full-scope-report
outputs.desc: Complete list of affected systems, data, and services

outputs.name: data-impact-assessment
outputs.desc: Classification of encrypted data by sensitivity and business criticality

process: Scan the network for indicators of compromise on systems not yet identified
Inventory all encrypted files and classify by data type and sensitivity
Determine which business services are impacted and their recovery priority
Estimate the timeline of the attack from initial access to encryption

steps.description: Evaluate all recovery options and select the best path forward.

inputs.name: full-scope-report
inputs.desc: Complete scope of the ransomware impact

outputs.name: recovery-plan
outputs.desc: Selected recovery approach with steps and timeline

outputs.name: backup-status
outputs.desc: Assessment of backup availability and integrity

process: Check backup availability and verify integrity for all affected systems
Search for public decryptors matching the identified ransomware variant
Assess whether shadow copies or other recovery points survived
Select the recovery path (restore from backup, use decryptor, or rebuild) and document the decision

steps.description: Execute the recovery plan to restore affected systems and data.

outputs.name: recovery-log
outputs.desc: Record of all restoration actions and their outcomes

outputs.name: restored-systems-list
outputs.desc: List of systems restored and their verification status

process: Rebuild or reimage affected systems from clean media
Restore data from verified backups, applying the most recent clean backup
Patch and harden systems before reconnecting to the network
Verify each restored system is functional and free of malware

steps.description: Produce the final ransomware incident response report with timeline, impact, and lessons learned.

outputs.name: ransomware-ir-report
outputs.desc: Complete incident response report

outputs.name: remediation-actions
outputs.desc: List of follow-up actions to prevent recurrence

process: Compile the full timeline from detection through recovery
Summarize the business impact (downtime, data loss, financial cost)
Document root cause and initial access vector
List remediation actions to prevent recurrence with owners and deadlines

description: Respond to a phishing incident from report intake through credential reset and infrastructure blocking.

steps.description: Receive and triage a reported phishing email.

inputs.name: reported-email
inputs.desc: The phishing email sample or report from the user

inputs.name: reporter-info
inputs.desc: Who reported the email and when

outputs.name: triage-result
outputs.desc: Initial classification: confirmed phishing, suspicious, or benign

outputs.name: email-metadata
outputs.desc: Extracted headers, sender, subject, timestamp

process: Extract and record email headers, sender address, subject, and body
Check the sender against known threat intelligence feeds
Classify the email as confirmed phishing, suspicious, or benign
If confirmed or suspicious, escalate to full investigation

steps.description: Analyze the phishing email content, links, and attachments in a sandbox.

outputs.name: ioc-list
outputs.desc: Indicators of compromise: URLs, domains, IPs, file hashes

outputs.name: payload-analysis
outputs.desc: Analysis of any malicious attachments or landing pages

process: Detonate any attachments in a sandbox environment and record behavior
Follow links in an isolated browser and capture the landing page
Extract all indicators of compromise (URLs, domains, IPs, file hashes)
Determine the attack objective (credential harvesting, malware delivery, BEC)

steps.description: Identify all recipients who received the phishing email and who interacted with it.

inputs.name: email-metadata
inputs.desc: Sender, subject, and other matching criteria

inputs.name: ioc-list
inputs.desc: URLs and domains from the phishing email

outputs.name: recipient-list
outputs.desc: All users who received the phishing email

outputs.name: interaction-list
outputs.desc: Users who clicked links, opened attachments, or submitted credentials

process: Search the mail system for all deliveries matching the phishing email (sender, subject, message-ID)
Check web proxy or DNS logs for connections to the phishing URLs
Check endpoint telemetry for attachment execution
Compile the list of users who received and who interacted

steps.description: Reset credentials and revoke sessions for users who submitted credentials to the phishing site.

inputs.name: interaction-list
inputs.desc: Users who clicked or submitted credentials

inputs.name: ioc-list
inputs.desc: Phishing URLs and domains for context

outputs.name: reset-log
outputs.desc: Record of all credential resets and session revocations

outputs.name: user-notifications
outputs.desc: Notifications sent to affected users

process: Force password reset for all users who submitted credentials
Revoke all active sessions and OAuth tokens for affected accounts
Enable or verify MFA on affected accounts
Notify each affected user with instructions

steps.description: Block the phishing infrastructure across all defensive layers.

inputs.name: ioc-list
inputs.desc: URLs, domains, IPs, and hashes to block

inputs.name: reset-log
inputs.desc: Confirmation that affected accounts are secured

outputs.name: block-confirmation
outputs.desc: Record of all blocks applied across systems

outputs.name: detection-rules
outputs.desc: New detection rules created for this campaign

process: Block phishing domains and IPs at the firewall and web proxy
Add file hashes to endpoint detection blocklists
Create mail transport rules to quarantine matching future emails
Write detection rules for the phishing campaign TTPs

steps.description: Produce the phishing incident response report with impact assessment and recommendations.

inputs.name: block-confirmation
inputs.desc: Record of all defensive actions taken

inputs.name: interaction-list
inputs.desc: Users who interacted with the phishing email

outputs.name: phishing-ir-report
outputs.desc: Complete phishing incident response report

outputs.name: awareness-recommendations
outputs.desc: Targeted training recommendations based on the incident

process: Compile the timeline from delivery through containment
Summarize the impact (number of recipients, number who interacted, credentials compromised)
Document the phishing TTPs and indicators for threat intelligence sharing
Recommend targeted awareness training for users who interacted

description: Respond to a confirmed data breach from initial assessment through regulatory notification and reporting.

steps.description: Confirm the data breach and assess the types and volume of data exposed.

inputs.name: breach-indicators
inputs.desc: Initial indicators that a data breach occurred

inputs.name: system-context
inputs.desc: Systems involved and their data classifications

outputs.name: breach-confirmation
outputs.desc: Confirmed breach with data types and exposure method

outputs.name: data-inventory
outputs.desc: Inventory of exposed data types, volumes, and sensitivity levels

process: Investigate the indicators to confirm unauthorized data access or exfiltration
Identify all data types exposed (PII, PHI, financial, credentials, trade secrets)
Estimate the volume of records and number of affected individuals
Determine the method of exposure (exfiltration, misconfiguration, lost device)

steps.description: Investigate the full scope of the breach including timeline and access patterns.

inputs.name: data-inventory
inputs.desc: Types and volumes of exposed data

outputs.name: scope-findings
outputs.desc: Full scope including timeline, access patterns, and attacker methods

outputs.name: affected-individual-count
outputs.desc: Number and categories of affected data subjects

process: Analyze logs to determine the earliest point of unauthorized access
Map all systems and data stores the attacker accessed
Identify the exfiltration method and volume of data taken
Determine the number and categories of affected individuals

steps.description: Preserve all evidence related to the breach for investigation and potential legal proceedings.

outputs.name: evidence-package
outputs.desc: Preserved and cataloged evidence with chain of custody

outputs.name: forensic-timeline
outputs.desc: Reconstructed timeline of attacker activity

process: Preserve all relevant logs, disk images, and memory captures
Hash and catalog each evidence item with chain-of-custody documentation
Build the forensic timeline from all available evidence sources
Store evidence in a secure location with access controls and audit logging

steps.description: Coordinate with legal counsel and compliance on notification obligations.

inputs.name: data-inventory
inputs.desc: Types of data exposed and jurisdictions affected

inputs.name: affected-individual-count
inputs.desc: Number and categories of affected individuals

outputs.name: notification-requirements
outputs.desc: List of regulatory and contractual notification obligations with deadlines

outputs.name: legal-guidance
outputs.desc: Legal counsel guidance on disclosure and liability

process: Identify all applicable breach notification laws by jurisdiction (GDPR, state laws, HIPAA)
Determine contractual notification obligations to partners and customers
Calculate notification deadlines for each jurisdiction
Obtain legal guidance on disclosure scope and liability exposure

steps.description: Prepare and submit regulatory notifications within required timelines.

inputs.name: scope-findings
inputs.desc: Full scope of the breach for notification content

outputs.name: regulatory-submissions
outputs.desc: Filed regulatory notifications with confirmation receipts

outputs.name: notification-log
outputs.desc: Log of all notifications sent with dates and recipients

process: Draft regulatory notifications following each jurisdiction's required format
Include all required elements (data types, affected count, remediation steps, contact info)
Submit notifications within the required timelines
Document all submissions with confirmation receipts

steps.description: Prepare and send notifications to affected individuals.

inputs.name: affected-individual-count
inputs.desc: Number and contact information for affected individuals

inputs.name: legal-guidance
inputs.desc: Legal requirements for individual notification content

outputs.name: individual-notifications
outputs.desc: Sent notifications to affected individuals

outputs.name: support-resources
outputs.desc: Credit monitoring or identity protection services offered

process: Draft individual notification letters following legal requirements
Include a description of the breach, data types exposed, and protective steps to take
Arrange credit monitoring or identity protection services if warranted
Send notifications and document delivery

steps.description: Produce the final data breach response report.

outputs.name: breach-response-report
outputs.desc: Complete data breach response report

outputs.name: prevention-recommendations
outputs.desc: Recommendations to prevent similar breaches

process: Compile the complete timeline from initial access through notification
Summarize the total impact (individuals affected, data types, financial cost)
Document all response actions and their effectiveness
List recommendations to prevent recurrence

description: Investigate a suspected insider threat from initial referral through evidence documentation and reporting.

steps.description: Receive and assess the insider threat referral and its supporting indicators.

inputs.name: referral-details
inputs.desc: The insider threat referral with initial indicators

inputs.name: subject-role-info
inputs.desc: Subject's role, access level, and organizational context

outputs.name: investigation-scope
outputs.desc: Defined scope and objectives of the investigation

outputs.name: initial-risk-assessment
outputs.desc: Preliminary risk level based on the indicators

process: Review the referral and classify the type of insider threat (theft, sabotage, espionage, negligence)
Assess the subject's access level and potential for harm
Define the investigation scope, objectives, and legal boundaries
Coordinate with legal and HR before proceeding

steps.description: Preserve all relevant logs and access records for the investigation subject.

inputs.name: investigation-scope
inputs.desc: Scope and subject of the investigation

inputs.name: subject-role-info
inputs.desc: Systems and data the subject has access to

outputs.name: preserved-logs
outputs.desc: Preserved access logs, email logs, and system activity for the subject

outputs.name: preservation-receipt
outputs.desc: Chain-of-custody documentation for preserved data

process: Place a legal hold on all relevant logs and communications for the subject
Collect authentication logs, VPN logs, and badge access records
Preserve email and messaging archives for the investigation period
Document all preservation actions with timestamps and chain of custody

steps.description: Analyze the subject's data access patterns for anomalies.

inputs.name: initial-risk-assessment
inputs.desc: Preliminary risk level and indicators to investigate

outputs.name: access-anomalies
outputs.desc: Identified anomalous access patterns with evidence

outputs.name: data-access-timeline
outputs.desc: Timeline of the subject's data access activity

process: Build a baseline of the subject's normal access patterns
Identify deviations from baseline (unusual hours, volumes, file types, systems)
Cross-reference with known indicators from the referral
Build a timeline of suspicious activity

steps.description: Check for data exfiltration indicators across all available channels.

outputs.name: exfiltration-findings
outputs.desc: Evidence of data exfiltration or lack thereof

outputs.name: channel-analysis
outputs.desc: Analysis of each potential exfiltration channel

process: Check USB and removable media logs for large file copies
Review email and messaging for outbound file transfers
Check cloud storage sync activity (personal cloud, file sharing)
Analyze network traffic for unusual outbound data volumes

steps.description: Coordinate findings with HR and legal for appropriate response.

inputs.name: exfiltration-findings
inputs.desc: Evidence of exfiltration or other insider activity

outputs.name: response-decision
outputs.desc: Decision on employment action, legal referral, or monitoring

outputs.name: coordination-log
outputs.desc: Record of all HR and legal consultations

process: Present findings to HR and legal with supporting evidence
Assess whether the evidence supports employment action, legal referral, or continued monitoring
Determine whether law enforcement notification is appropriate
Document all decisions and their rationale

steps.description: Document the investigation findings with evidence for the insider threat report.

outputs.name: insider-threat-report
outputs.desc: Complete insider threat investigation report

outputs.name: prevention-controls
outputs.desc: Recommended controls to prevent similar incidents

process: Compile all evidence into a structured investigation report
Include the timeline, findings, and supporting evidence for each finding
Document the response decision and its rationale
Recommend controls to detect and prevent similar insider threats

description: Respond to a distributed denial-of-service attack from detection through mitigation and post-attack analysis.

steps.description: Detect and classify the DDoS attack by type and characteristics.

inputs.name: network-alerts
inputs.desc: Network monitoring alerts indicating abnormal traffic

inputs.name: service-status
inputs.desc: Status of affected services and their degradation level

outputs.name: attack-classification
outputs.desc: Attack type (volumetric, protocol, application layer) and characteristics

outputs.name: traffic-profile
outputs.desc: Profile of attack traffic including sources, protocols, and volume

process: Confirm the service degradation is caused by a DDoS attack, not an infrastructure failure
Classify the attack type: volumetric (bandwidth flood), protocol (SYN flood, amplification), or application layer (HTTP flood)
Profile the attack traffic: source distribution, protocols, packet sizes, and request patterns
Estimate the attack volume in Gbps or requests per second

steps.description: Activate DDoS mitigation measures to restore service availability.

inputs.name: attack-classification
inputs.desc: Type and characteristics of the DDoS attack

inputs.name: traffic-profile
inputs.desc: Profile of attack traffic for filtering rules

outputs.name: mitigation-status
outputs.desc: Status of activated mitigation measures

outputs.name: filtering-rules
outputs.desc: Applied traffic filtering and rate limiting rules

process: Activate scrubbing services or DDoS mitigation provider if available
Apply rate limiting rules targeted at the attack traffic profile
Implement geo-blocking if attack sources are concentrated in specific regions
Enable application-layer protections (CAPTCHA, JavaScript challenges) for application-layer attacks

steps.description: Coordinate with upstream providers and ISPs for additional mitigation support.

inputs.name: mitigation-status
inputs.desc: Current mitigation measures and their effectiveness

inputs.name: traffic-profile
inputs.desc: Attack traffic details for upstream filtering

outputs.name: upstream-actions
outputs.desc: Actions taken by upstream providers

outputs.name: escalation-log
outputs.desc: Record of all provider communications and requests

process: Contact the ISP or hosting provider with attack details and request upstream filtering
Engage the CDN provider to absorb volumetric attack traffic
Request blackhole routing for specific attack source prefixes if needed
Document all communications and actions taken by each provider

steps.description: Monitor the effectiveness of mitigation measures and adjust as needed.

inputs.name: filtering-rules
inputs.desc: Current filtering and rate limiting rules

outputs.name: mitigation-effectiveness
outputs.desc: Assessment of how well mitigations are working

outputs.name: adjusted-rules
outputs.desc: Updated rules based on monitoring results

process: Monitor service availability and response times during mitigation
Track the ratio of legitimate to attack traffic being passed
Adjust filtering rules if the attacker changes tactics
Document mitigation effectiveness metrics over time

steps.description: Analyze the attack sources and attempt attribution if possible.

outputs.name: source-analysis
outputs.desc: Analysis of attack sources (botnet, amplification reflectors, origin)

outputs.name: attribution-findings
outputs.desc: Any attribution indicators identified

process: Analyze source IP distribution for botnet characteristics
Check for amplification reflectors (DNS, NTP, memcached) being abused
Look for patterns that indicate the attack tool or service used
Document any attribution indicators for potential law enforcement referral

steps.description: Plan defenses against recurrence based on lessons from the attack.

inputs.name: adjusted-rules
inputs.desc: Effective filtering rules from the incident

outputs.name: recurrence-plan
outputs.desc: Plan for defending against future attacks of this type

outputs.name: ddos-ir-report
outputs.desc: Complete DDoS incident response report

process: Document the effective mitigation techniques for this attack type
Update the DDoS response runbook with lessons learned
Implement permanent protections based on the attack profile
Produce the final DDoS incident response report with timeline and recommendations

description: Respond to a compromised user account from confirmation through remediation and reporting.

steps.description: Confirm that the account is compromised by analyzing the indicators.

inputs.name: compromise-indicators
inputs.desc: Alerts or reports suggesting account compromise

inputs.name: account-details
inputs.desc: Account username, role, and access level

outputs.name: compromise-confirmation
outputs.desc: Confirmed compromise with evidence and method of access

outputs.name: indicator-summary
outputs.desc: Summary of all compromise indicators identified

process: Review the indicators (impossible travel, unusual login location, anomalous activity)
Check authentication logs for unauthorized access patterns
Verify with the account owner whether the activity was legitimate
Confirm the compromise and document the evidence

steps.description: Disable the compromised account and revoke all active sessions.

outputs.name: lockdown-log
outputs.desc: Record of all account lockdown actions

outputs.name: session-revocation
outputs.desc: Confirmation that all active sessions are terminated

process: Disable the account or force a sign-out across all sessions
Revoke all OAuth tokens, API keys, and refresh tokens
Disable any app passwords or legacy authentication methods
Document each lockdown action with timestamp

steps.description: Assess what the attacker accessed or modified while using the compromised account.

inputs.name: lockdown-log
inputs.desc: Confirmation the account is locked down

outputs.name: impact-assessment
outputs.desc: List of data and systems accessed by the attacker

outputs.name: attacker-activity-timeline
outputs.desc: Timeline of attacker actions in the account

process: Review audit logs for all actions taken during the compromise window
Identify emails read, sent, or forwarded by the attacker
Check for data downloads, file access, or modifications
Determine if the attacker used the account to pivot to other systems

steps.description: Check for persistence mechanisms the attacker may have installed.

outputs.name: persistence-findings
outputs.desc: Any persistence mechanisms found and removed

outputs.name: cleanup-log
outputs.desc: Record of all persistence removal actions

process: Check for email forwarding rules or inbox rules created by the attacker
Review OAuth application grants for unauthorized third-party apps
Check for API keys or service credentials created during the compromise
Remove any identified persistence mechanisms and document each removal

steps.description: Reset credentials and restore the account with strengthened security.

outputs.name: restoration-confirmation
outputs.desc: Account restored with new credentials and security controls

outputs.name: user-notification
outputs.desc: Notification sent to the account owner

process: Reset the account password to a new strong credential
Enable or verify multi-factor authentication
Re-enable the account and verify the owner can access it
Notify the account owner with details of the incident and protective steps taken

steps.description: Produce the account compromise incident report.

outputs.name: account-compromise-report
outputs.desc: Complete account compromise incident report

outputs.name: prevention-recommendations
outputs.desc: Recommendations to prevent future account compromises

process: Compile the timeline from initial compromise through restoration
Summarize the impact (data accessed, actions taken by the attacker)
Document the root cause (phishing, credential stuffing, password reuse)
Recommend prevention measures (MFA enforcement, conditional access policies)

description: Conduct a blameless post-incident review to identify root causes and improvement actions.

steps.description: Gather the complete incident timeline from all responders and systems.

inputs.name: incident-id
inputs.desc: Identifier for the incident being reviewed

inputs.name: responder-list
inputs.desc: List of all personnel who responded to the incident

outputs.name: raw-timeline
outputs.desc: Collected timeline entries from all sources

outputs.name: evidence-references
outputs.desc: References to logs, tickets, and communications from the incident

process: Collect timeline entries from each responder (what they did and when)
Gather timestamps from monitoring systems, tickets, and communication channels
Collect any screenshots, log excerpts, or other evidence from the response
Merge all entries into a single chronological timeline

steps.description: Document a clear narrative of what happened during the incident.

inputs.name: raw-timeline
inputs.desc: Collected timeline entries from all sources

outputs.name: incident-narrative
outputs.desc: Clear narrative of what happened and when

outputs.name: key-decisions-log
outputs.desc: Record of key decisions made during the response and their context

process: Write a clear chronological narrative from the merged timeline
Identify and document key decision points and what information was available at each
Note where the response diverged from established procedures
Validate the narrative with the responders for accuracy

steps.description: Assess what went well and what did not during the incident response.

outputs.name: went-well-list
outputs.desc: Actions and processes that worked effectively

outputs.name: improvement-areas
outputs.desc: Areas where the response could have been better

process: Identify actions that reduced impact or accelerated recovery
Identify delays, miscommunications, or ineffective actions
Assess the effectiveness of tools, processes, and communication channels used
Frame findings as systemic issues, not individual blame

steps.description: Determine the root cause and contributing factors of the incident.

outputs.name: root-cause-finding
outputs.desc: Identified root cause with supporting evidence

outputs.name: contributing-factors
outputs.desc: List of factors that contributed to the incident or its severity

process: Apply root cause analysis techniques (5 Whys, fishbone diagram, fault tree)
Distinguish between the root cause and contributing factors
Identify systemic issues that allowed the incident to occur or worsen
Document the analysis with evidence supporting each finding

steps.description: Define remediation actions with owners, priorities, and deadlines.

outputs.name: remediation-actions
outputs.desc: Prioritized list of remediation actions with owners and deadlines

outputs.name: success-criteria
outputs.desc: Measurable criteria to verify each remediation is effective

process: Define specific actions to address the root cause
Define actions to address each contributing factor
Assign an owner and deadline to each action
Define measurable success criteria for each action

steps.description: Compile and share the post-incident review document and lessons learned.

outputs.name: post-incident-review-doc
outputs.desc: Complete post-incident review document

outputs.name: lessons-learned-summary
outputs.desc: Key lessons for broader distribution

process: Compile the post-incident review document with all sections
Write a lessons-learned summary for teams not directly involved
Schedule a follow-up review to verify remediation progress
Distribute the review to relevant stakeholders

description: Manage all incident communications to internal and external stakeholders.

steps.description: Identify all stakeholders who need to be notified about the incident.

inputs.name: incident-summary
inputs.desc: Summary of the incident including type, severity, and impact

outputs.name: stakeholder-list
outputs.desc: Categorized list of stakeholders requiring notification

outputs.name: notification-priorities
outputs.desc: Priority order for stakeholder notifications

process: Identify internal stakeholders (executives, IT, legal, HR, affected business units)
Identify external stakeholders (customers, regulators, partners, media)
Categorize by urgency and notification method
Set the notification priority order

steps.description: Draft internal communications for different audience levels.

inputs.name: stakeholder-list
inputs.desc: Internal stakeholders and their information needs

outputs.name: executive-briefing
outputs.desc: Briefing for executive leadership

outputs.name: staff-notification
outputs.desc: Notification for affected staff and IT teams

process: Draft an executive briefing with impact, response status, and decisions needed
Draft a technical briefing for IT and security staff
Draft a general notification for affected business units
Review all drafts with legal before distribution

steps.description: Draft external communications for customers, regulators, and media.

outputs.name: customer-notification
outputs.desc: Draft notification for affected customers

outputs.name: media-statement
outputs.desc: Prepared statement for media inquiries

process: Draft customer notification with incident details and protective steps
Draft regulatory notification if required
Prepare a holding statement for media inquiries
Review all external communications with legal counsel

steps.description: Coordinate with legal counsel on disclosure obligations and timing.

outputs.name: legal-approved-comms
outputs.desc: Communications approved by legal for release

outputs.name: disclosure-timeline
outputs.desc: Approved timeline for each disclosure

process: Review all draft communications with legal counsel
Confirm regulatory disclosure obligations and deadlines
Get legal approval on communication content and timing
Document the approved disclosure timeline

steps.description: Execute the communication plan according to the approved timeline.

outputs.name: distribution-log
outputs.desc: Record of all communications sent with timestamps

outputs.name: acknowledgment-tracking
outputs.desc: Tracking of receipt and acknowledgment from key stakeholders

process: Send internal notifications according to the priority order
Send external notifications according to the approved timeline
Track acknowledgment from key stakeholders
Document all distributions with timestamps and delivery confirmation

steps.description: Handle incoming inquiries from stakeholders and media during the incident.

inputs.name: distribution-log
inputs.desc: Record of what has been communicated

outputs.name: inquiry-log
outputs.desc: Record of all inquiries received and responses given

outputs.name: incident-communication-report
outputs.desc: Complete incident communication report

process: Log all incoming inquiries with source, question, and response
Route media inquiries to the designated spokesperson
Provide consistent responses aligned with approved communications
Compile the final incident communication report

description: Preserve digital evidence during a security incident for investigation and legal proceedings.

steps.description: Identify all relevant evidence sources for the incident.

inputs.name: incident-details
inputs.desc: Description of the incident and systems involved

inputs.name: affected-systems
inputs.desc: List of systems potentially containing evidence

outputs.name: evidence-source-list
outputs.desc: Prioritized list of all evidence sources to collect

outputs.name: collection-plan
outputs.desc: Plan for collecting evidence in priority order

process: Inventory all systems that may contain relevant evidence
Categorize evidence sources by volatility (memory > disk > network > logs)
Prioritize collection based on volatility (most volatile first)
Create a collection plan with responsible personnel for each source

steps.description: Capture volatile data before it is lost due to system shutdown or reboot.

inputs.name: affected-systems
inputs.desc: Systems to capture volatile data from

outputs.name: memory-captures
outputs.desc: Memory dumps from affected systems

outputs.name: volatile-state
outputs.desc: Running processes, network connections, and logged-in users

process: Capture physical memory using forensic tools (WinPmem, LiME, FTK Imager)
Record running processes, open files, and loaded modules
Capture active network connections and listening ports
Record logged-in users and active sessions

steps.description: Create forensic images of affected storage media.

inputs.name: collection-plan
inputs.desc: Collection plan identifying disks to image

inputs.name: volatile-state
inputs.desc: Volatile data already captured (safe to proceed with disk)

outputs.name: disk-images
outputs.desc: Forensic disk images with verification hashes

outputs.name: imaging-log
outputs.desc: Record of imaging process including tool, time, and hashes

process: Connect a write blocker to prevent modification of the source media
Create a bit-for-bit forensic image using dd, FTK Imager, or equivalent
Compute and record cryptographic hashes (SHA-256) of the source and image
Verify the image hash matches the source hash

steps.description: Collect logs from all relevant systems and aggregate them.

inputs.name: incident-details
inputs.desc: Incident details for scoping log collection

outputs.name: collected-logs
outputs.desc: Aggregated logs from all relevant sources

outputs.name: log-inventory
outputs.desc: Inventory of collected logs with sources, date ranges, and formats

process: Collect authentication and access logs from identity systems
Collect firewall, proxy, and network device logs
Collect application and database logs from affected services
Export SIEM alerts and correlation data for the incident timeframe

steps.description: Hash and catalog all collected evidence items.

outputs.name: evidence-catalog
outputs.desc: Complete catalog of all evidence items with hashes and metadata

outputs.name: chain-of-custody-forms
outputs.desc: Chain-of-custody documentation for each evidence item

process: Compute SHA-256 hashes for every evidence item
Create a catalog entry for each item (source, type, size, hash, collection time, collector)
Fill out chain-of-custody forms for each item
Assign unique evidence identifiers to each item

steps.description: Store evidence securely with access controls and integrity verification.

outputs.name: storage-confirmation
outputs.desc: Confirmation that all evidence is securely stored

outputs.name: evidence-inventory-report
outputs.desc: Final evidence inventory with storage locations

process: Transfer evidence to a secure storage location (encrypted, access-controlled)
Restrict access to authorized investigators only
Enable audit logging on the evidence storage
